column5: Area of Degraded Land Under Sustainable Management
column6: number of hectares of the target land that is effectively managed by formal and informal natural resources protection measures
column7: nombre d'hectares des terres ciblées qui sont gérées efficacement par des mesures formelles et informelles de protection des ressources naturelles
column10: The indicator assesses the total area of degraded land (including forests, pastures, fields, etc.) that is effectively protected against further degradation. The protection can be ensured by community bylaws, regulations enforced by relevant authorities, individual farmers applying soil protection measures and other means.

column6: at least X out of Y Landscape Management Plans fulfilled the required minimum of their targets
column7: au moins X plans de gestion du paysage sur Y ont atteint le minimum requis de leurs objectifs
column10: A Landscape Management Plan is a document outlining what will be done, by whom and by when, to rehabilitate and protect natural resources in a given area. The Plans are designed in close cooperation between local community members, extension workers and the relevant authorities. The indicator assesses the number of Landscape Management Plans which achieved a minimum proportion of their targets set for a given period (usually several months before a project ends).

column6: number of communities with an effective natural resources management structure in place
column7: nombre de collectivités ayant une structure de gestion des ressources naturelles efficace
column10: The indicator assesses the number of communities with an effective system for managing their local natural resources.

column6: number or % of farmers who for the past [specify the duration] correctly followed the promoted [specify: climate-smart / sustainable / other] agronomic practices
column7: nombre ou % d'agriculteurs qui au cours des derniers [précisez la durée] ont correctement suivi les pratiques agronomiques promues [précisez: climato-compatibles/ durables / autres]
column10: The indicator measures the extent to which the target group members correctly use the desired climate-smart / sustainable / environmentally friendly / other agronomic practices (such as practices reducing erosion / retaining water in soil / increasing the content of nutrients in an environmentally friendly manner, etc.). The fulfillment of such an indicator is among the main pre-conditions for achieving the desired outcomes of agricultural interventions.

column6: number of hectares of agriculture land in the project target area affected by surface erosion
column7: nombre d'hectares de terres agricoles affectées par l'érosion de surface dans les zones cibles du projet
column10: The indicator quantifies the total area of the targeted agricultural land that is affected by surface erosion. When using the indicator, focus only on those productive agricultural lands (fields, pastures and forests) where recent farming practices caused surface erosion (which your intervention aimed to reduce).

column5: Functionality of the Water Management Groups
column6: number or % of targeted water management groups performing at least X% of their core functions
column7: nombre ou % de groupes de gestion de l'eau ciblés réalisant au moins X% de leurs fonctions essentielles
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion/ number of targeted water management groups who perform a certain percentage of their responsibilities - a crucial precondition for ensuring the local water sources' sustainability.

column6: number or % of trained farmers who in the past [specify the time period] tried [specify the promoted agronomic practice] on their farms
column7: nombre ou % d'agriculteurs formés qui, dans le passé [spécifier la période], ont essayé [précisez la pratique agronomique promue] dans leurs fermes
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion or number of trained farmers who tried an agronomic practice promoted by your intervention on their own farms. It indicates the extent to which farmers are interested in its use.

column6: % beneficiaries considering that their basic WASH needs are met
column7: % de bénéficiaires considérant que leurs besoins de base en matière d’EHA sont satisfaits
column10: This sub-indicator was designed by ECHO as a part of its Key Outcome Indicators (KOI). It measures the proportion of the target population who perceive that their most essential WASH needs were met.

column5: Awareness of the Causes and Prevention of Diarrhoea
column6: % of respondents who know at least three of the main causes of diarrhoea and three ways to prevent diarrhoea
column7: % de répondants capables d'indiquer trois des causes principales de la diarrhée et trois manières d’éviter la diarrhée
column10: The indicator assesses the extent to which the target population is aware of at least three causes of diarrhoea and three ways to prevent diarrhoea. It is commonly used for measuring the immediate results of hygiene promotion activities.

column5: Coverage of Solid Waste Management System
column6: number of people living in settlements with a functional solid waste management system
column7: nombre de personnes vivant dans des localités ayant un système fonctionnel de gestion des déchets solides
column10: The indicator measures the number of people who live in areas with functional solid waste removal services. “Functionality” is determined by three main aspects.

column6: % of caregivers who safely dispose of their children's faeces
column7: % de gardiens d’enfants qui s’occupent en toute sécurité des fèces de leurs enfants
column10: Even in households with access to latrines, children's faeces are often not disposed of safely and threaten both children's and adults' health. This indicator therefore assesses the proportion of caregivers who dispose of the children's faeces into improved sanitation facility.

column6: % of households who keep their sanitation facilities clean
column7: % de ménages qui maintiennent leurs installations d'assainissement propres
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of households who keep their latrines clean - an essential precondition for their use and for ensuring effective vector control.

column5: Prevention of Groundwater Contamination by Faeces
column6: % of latrines located at least 30m away from any ground water source and their pit bottoms being at least 1.5m above the water table
column7: % de latrines situées à au moins 30 m de toute source d'eau souterraine et dont le fond est au moins 1,5 m au-dessus de la nappe phréatique
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of latrines (or other excreta containment measures) located so as to prevent human faecal contamination of the local water sources.

column6: % of households that safely dispose of their solid waste
column7: % de ménages qui jettent leurs déchets solides d'une manière sûre
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of households which dispose of their solid waste in a way that does not threaten human and environmental health (which can occur, for example, from the breeding of flies and rodents or from polluting water sources).

column6: % of households using basic sanitation services
column7: % de ménages utilisant une installation d'assainissement améliorée
column10: This indicator assesses the proportion of households using basic sanitation services - one of the most effective measures for preventing diarrhoea and other life-threatening diseases.

column6: % of users considering basic WASH services to be functional in the target facilities
column7: % d'utilisateurs considérant que les services EHA de base sont fonctionnels dans les installations ciblées
column10: This indicator measures the proportion of the target facilities’ users (such as health centres’ patients or schools’ students) that consider the facilities’ basic WASH services to be functional (in terms of its quality, quantity and access).

column6: number or % of persons with adequate and safe access to bathing facilities
column7: nombre ou % de personnes ayant un accès adéquat et sûr aux installations de bain
column10: The indicator measures the number or proportion of persons with an adequate and safe access to bathing facilities. This indicator is mostly used in the context of camps/ collective settlement.

column6: number or % of people with access to dignified, safe, clean and functional excreta disposal facilities
column7: nombre ou % de personnes ayant accès à des installations de gestion des excréments dignes, sûres, propres et fonctionnelles
column10: The composite indicator measures the affected population's access to a sufficient number of safely located latrines with functioning hand washing facilities - a crucial precondition for ensuring a sanitary environment and preventing diseases.

column5: Access to Sanitation Facilities at Institutions
column6: % of targeted institutions with accessible improved sanitation facilities
column7: % des institutions cibles disposant d’installations sanitaires améliorées
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of targeted institutions (such as schools, health centres, administration buildings, evacuation sites) with accessible improved sanitation facilities.

column6: number or % of target schools with separate improved sanitation facilities for boys and girls
column7: nombre ou % d’écoles ciblées disposant d’installations sanitaires améliorées et séparées pour les garçons et les filles
column10: Ensuring sanitation facilities at schools are comfortable and safe to use for both boys and girls is one of the pre-conditions for increasing girls’ school attendance. This indicator therefore measures the number (or proportion) of the target schools that have separate improved sanitation for boys and girls.

column6: number of households who built their own latrine according to the provided "model latrine"
column7: nombre de ménages qui ont construit leurs propres latrines selon le "modèle de latrine" fourni
column10: The indicator assesses the number of households who constructed their own latrine according to the "model latrine" example promoted by a company, non-governmental organization or local authority.

column6: % of WASH promoters that passed both theoretical and practical test
column7: % des promoteurs EHA qui ont réussi à la fois les tests théoriques et pratiques
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of persons responsible for promoting hygiene/ water /sanitation-related behaviours that have the required knowledge and skills. The "promoters" can be volunteers, health workers but also school teachers or other influential community members.

column6: number of people living in settlements with a functional solid waste management system
column7: nombre de personnes vivant dans des sites ayant un système fonctionnel de gestion des déchets solides
column10: The indicator measures the number of people who live in areas with functional solid waste removal services. “Functionality” is determined by three main aspects.

column6: % beneficiaries considering that their basic WASH needs are met
column7: % de bénéficiaires considérant que leurs besoins de base en matière d’EHA sont satisfaits
column10: This sub-indicator was designed by ECHO as a part of its Key Outcome Indicators (KOI). It measures the proportion of the target population who perceive that their most essential WASH needs were met.

column6: number or % of the target households using basic drinking water services
column7: nombre ou % de ménages utilisant de l'eau potable provenant d'une source sûre
column10: Waterborne diseases are among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among children. The indicator therefore assesses the proportion of the target households using drinking water from an improved source whose distance is not more than 30 minutes for a roundtrip including queuing.

column5: Average Queuing Time at a Water Point
column6: the average queuing time at the target water points
column7: le temps moyen d'attente aux sources d'eau ciblées
column10: The indicator measures the average time the respondents spend between arriving at the water source and starting to fill their water container. Excessive queuing times are indicators of insufficient water availability due to either an inadequate number of water points or their insufficient yields.

column5: Awareness of the Causes and Prevention of Diarrhoea
column6: % of respondents who know at least three of the main causes of diarrhoea and three ways to prevent diarrhoea
column7: % de répondants capables d'indiquer trois des causes principales de la diarrhée et trois manières d’éviter la diarrhée
column10: The indicator assesses the extent to which the target population is aware of at least three causes of diarrhoea and three ways to prevent diarrhoea. It is commonly used for measuring the immediate results of hygiene promotion activities.

column6: average time required to reach the water source, collect water (including queuing), and bring it back home
column7: temps moyen nécessaire pour atteindre un point d’eau, collecter de l’eau (incluant le temps d’attente), et ramener l’eau au domicile
column10: The indicator measures the average time household members need to go to their water source, collect water (including the waiting time), and bring it back home. The distance to the water source is a robust independent predictor of disease risk in that household (a 15-minute decrease in one-way walking time to the water source is associated with a 41% average relative reduction in diarrhoea prevalence*).

column6: average duration of the target water sources' functionality in the past 12 months
column7: durée moyenne de fonctionnement des sources d'eau ciblés au cours des 12 derniers mois
column10: The indicator assesses for how many months the target water sources in the past 12 months have been fully functional (i.e. provided the usual amount of water). It is an important sign of the water sources’ technical quality and maintenance.

column5: Number of People per Water Point
column6: number or % of supported communities not exceeding the maximum recommended number of people per water point
column7: nombre ou % de communautés appuyées n'excédant pas le nombre maximum recommandé de personnes par source d'eau
column10: This emergency indicator assesses whether the number (and capacity) of the local water points is sufficient for the number of people who use them.

column5: Prevention of Groundwater Contamination by Faeces
column6: % of latrines located at least 30m away from any ground water source and their pit bottoms being at least 1.5m above the water table
column7: % de latrines situées à au moins 30 m de toute source d'eau souterraine et dont le fond est au moins 1,5 m au-dessus de la nappe phréatique
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of latrines (or other excreta containment measures) located so as to prevent human faecal contamination of the local water sources.

column6: % of households who store their drinking water safely in clean containers
column7: % de ménages qui gardent l’eau en lieu sûr dans des récipients propres
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of households storing drinking water in a way that protects its quality and prevents contamination.

column6: % of households effectively treating their drinking water
column7: % de ménages traitant efficacement leur eau potable
column10: Unsafe water is among the main sources of life-threatening, waterborne diseases. This indicator therefore assesses the prevalence of households using effective methods for treating drinking water.

column6: number or % of targeted [specify the target group] using the promoted [specify the energy technology]
column7: nombre ou % de [spécifiez le groupe cible] ayant recours à la [spécifiez la technologie énergétique promue
column10: The indicator measures the number (or proportion) of the target group members that use the promoted types of climate-smart energy technologies. This includes technologies that either serve as eco-friendly sources of energy (solar lamps or biodigesters) or those that reduce the consumption of environmentally unsustainable energy sources (such as fuel-efficient stoves or housing insulation).

column6: % of users considering basic WASH services to be functional in the target facilities
column7: % d'utilisateurs considérant que les services EHA de base sont fonctionnels dans les installations ciblées
column10: This indicator measures the proportion of the target facilities’ users (such as health centres’ patients or schools’ students) that consider the facilities’ basic WASH services to be functional (in terms of its quality, quantity and access).

column6: % of girls and women stating that they feel safe when accessing water
column7: % de filles et de femmes affirmant qu’elles se sentent en sécurité pendant qu’elles collectent de l’eau
column10: Gender-based violence is one of the factors decreasing women’s (and households’ in general) access to water. The indicator therefore assesses the proportion of women and girls who feel safe when going to collect water.

column6: % of households capable of purchasing the safe water they need
column7: % de ménages capables d'acheter l'eau dont ils ont besoin
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of households capable of paying for the minimum amount of water their members need. Water affordability is a crucial pre-condition for ensuring adequate access to safe water.

column6: % of households with at least 15 litres of safe water for drinking, cooking and personal hygiene per person per day
column7: % de ménages disposant d'au moins 15 litres d'eau potable pour la consommation, la cuisine et l'hygiène personnelle par personne et par jour
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of households whose members collect a sufficient quantity of safe water for meeting their needs (the amount of 15 litres is based on the Sphere Standards).

column6: number or % of water sources operational (at the time of the survey)
column7: nombre ou % de sources d'eau opérationnelles (au moment de l'enquête)
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of water sources that are fully operational and provide their users with the usual amount of water.

column6: % of water management committees capable of ensuring the water source's repair
column7: % de comités de gestion de l'eau capables d'assurer la réparation de la source d'eau
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of water management committees (or other actors responsible for the water source's operation) capable of ensuring required repairs without unnecessary delays, when required.

column6: % of target water source users who are satisfied with the performance of the water management committees
column7: % d'utilisateurs des sources d'eau satisfaits du travail du comité de gestion de l'eau
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of people who are satisfied with the way in which the water management committees operate and maintain the local water sources (incl. their accessibility, pricing, etc.).

column6: % of [specify the target group] who follow the promoted water-saving measures
column7: % de [préciser le groupe cible] qui suivent les mesures d'économie d'eau promues
column10: This indicator measures the extent to which the target group members follow the promoted ways of using water more efficiently.

column5: Adequate WASH Services and Hygiene Practices
column6: % of target population with adequate WASH services and hygiene practices
column7: % de la population cible ayant des services WASH et des pratiques hygiéniques adéquats
column10: This indicator is one of ECHO's Key Outcome Indicators (KOI). It is a composite indicator (consisting of several sub-indicators) assessing the target group members' satisfaction with the extent to which their basic WASH needs are met and the extent to which they follow essential hygiene practices.

column5: Functionality of the Water Management Groups
column6: number or % of targeted water management groups performing at least X% of their core functions
column7: nombre ou % de groupes de gestion de l'eau ciblés réalisant au moins X% de leurs fonctions essentielles
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion/ number of targeted water management groups who perform a certain percentage of their responsibilities - a crucial precondition for ensuring the local water sources' sustainability.

column6: number or % of targeted [specify the institution] with year-round access to drinking water
column7: nombre ou % de [spécifier l’institution] ciblé(e)s ayant accès à l’eau potable pendant toute l’année
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of targeted institutions (such as schools, health centres, administration buildings, evacuation sites) with a year-round access to drinking water (i.e. water from a safe source).

column5: Handwashing Facilities With Soap and Water
column6: % of households with handwashing facilities with soap and water at home
column7: % de ménages ayant un lieu désigné pour le lavage des mains où l'eau et le savon sont présents
column10: Existing research shows that people with access to a handwashing facility are more likely to wash their hands. Furthermore, observation of handwashing materials by surveyors represents a more reliable proxy for measuring handwashing behaviour than asking individuals to report their own behaviour. This indicator therefore assesses the proportion of households with handwashing facilities with soap and water at home.

column6: % of WASH promoters that passed both theoretical and practical test
column7: % des promoteurs EHA qui ont réussi à la fois les tests théoriques et pratiques
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of persons responsible for promoting hygiene/ water /sanitation-related behaviours that have the required knowledge and skills. The "promoters" can be volunteers, health workers but also school teachers or other influential community members.

column6: Percentage of households (HH) reporting that all HH members have access to a safe, secure, clean, and well-maintained toilet, including water or anal cleansing materials
column7: Pourcentage de ménages (HH) déclarant que tous les membres du ménage ont accès à des toilettes sûres, sécurisées, propres et bien entretenues, avec de l’eau ou du matériel pour le nettoyage anal
column10: To measure sectoral outcomes of Cash & Voucher Assistance related to WASH, more specifically sanitation.

column6:
Percentage of households (HH) reporting that all HH members have access to an adequate 
quantity of safe water for drinking, cooking, personal and domestic hygiene
column7: Pourcentage de ménages (HH) déclarant que tous les membres du ménage ont accès à une quantité adéquate d’eau potable pour boire, cuisiner, assurer leur hygiène personnelle et domestique
column10: To measure sectoral outcomes of Cash & Voucher Assistance (CVA) related to WASH, more specifically water supply.

column5: Drinking Water Quality (fecal contamination, household level)
column6: % of households whose drinking water contains 0 fecal coliforms per 100 ml sample
column7: % de ménages ayant une eau potable ne contenant aucune bactérie coliforme fécale par échantillon de 100 ml
column10: The indicator assesses the presence of fecal coliforms in drinking water that was brought to the household. The presence of these harmful bacteria shows that the water has been contaminated by animal or human faeces.

column5: Drinking Water Quality (fecal contamination, water point level)
column6: % of targeted water points with 0 fecal coliforms per 100 ml sample
column7: % de sources d'eau ciblées ayant 0 bactérie coliforme fécale par échantillon de 100 ml
column10: The indicator assesses the presence of fecal coliforms in water at the water collection level. The presence of these harmful bacteria shows that the water has been contaminated by animal or human faeces.

column6: % of [select: targeted water points / household water samples] with free residual chlorine between 0.2 and 0.5 mg/l
column7: % de [sélectionner: points d’eau cibles/ échantillons d’eau domestique] contenant de 0.2 à 0.5 mg de chlore résiduel libre par litre
column10: This indicator measures if disinfection of the drinking water is correctly implemented at the source level or the household level.

column6: Percentage of group members reporting that capacity strengthening activities benefitted the group
column7: Pourcentage de membres du groupe déclarant que les activités de renforcement des capacités ont profité au groupe
column10: To measure to which extent the capacity strengthening activities have benefitted the group

column5: GCT Increased Capacity to Plan and Implement
column6: Percentage of supported groups reporting an increase in the capacity to design and successfully implement activities according to the communities’ priorities
column7: Pourcentage de groupes soutenus faisant état d'un renforcement de leur capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre avec succès des activités conformes aux priorités des communautés
column10: To measure to which extent the groups have increased their capacity to design and implement their own activities and plans.

column6: Percentage of groups that report being able to use the group cash transfer according to project plans (based on identified priority needs in the communities)
column7: Pourcentage de groupes qui déclarent être en mesure de dépenser les transferts d'argent du groupe conformément aux plans du projet (sur la base des besoins prioritaires identifiés dans les communautés)
column10: To measure to which extent groups are able to use the GCT to achieve their plans.

column6: Percent of group members reporting that group cash transfer support is delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable, and participatory manner
column7: Pourcentage de membres de groupes déclarant que les transferts monétaires de groupe sont effectués de manière sûre, accessible, responsable et participative.
column10: To measure to which extent the cash distribution process was delivered in an appropriate way

column6: Number of participants in group cash transfer co-design workshop
column7: Nombre de participants à l'atelier collectif de co-conception des transferts monétaires
column10: To measure how many people have participated in co-design and/or facilitation workshops.

column6: Total amount of cash grants provided to groups
column7: Montant total des subventions en espèces accordées aux groupes
column10: To measure the total expenditure of cash spent by the groups to achieve their objectives and implement their activities.

column6: Percentage of households who report being able to meet their basic needs as they define and prioritize them
column7: Pourcentage de ménages qui déclarent pouvoir répondre à leurs besoins de base, selon leurs définitions et priorités
column10:
You want a simple, cross-cutting means of gauging the extent to which overarching basic needs are being met, based on recipient perceptions (basic needs indicator).
You would also like a quantifiable means to better understand which needs are not being met, and the reasons for this, particularly in relation to household spending power and market functionality (follow up questions).
You would like to improve your understanding of the impact of the MPC on household expenditures and what it allows them to buy, or do, as compared to before they received the assistance (follow up questions)

column6: Percentage of households who report being able to meet specific basic needs, by category
column7: Pourcentage de ménages qui déclarent pouvoir répondre à des besoins de base spécifiques, par catégorie
column10:
You want to gain a more in-depth and quantified understanding of the extent to which recipients perceive they can meet specific basic needs, and of the reasons why these needs cannot be met, where this is the case. By extension, this also enables better analysis of where gaps in assistance may exist, and appropriate means of addressing them.
You have sufficient time and resources in terms of data collection and analysis, recognizing that this is a relatively more intensive and time-consuming option.

column6: Total monthly expenditures by sector relative to MEB sectoral components/amounts
column7: Dépenses mensuelles totales par secteur par rapport aux éléments/montants sectoriels du panier de dépenses minimum (MEB)
column10:
You want a comprehensive understanding of household expenditures and how they prioritize consumption, including total expenditure and spending by category. Categories/types of expenditure can correspond with different sectors.
You want to understand the extent to which total reported spending aligns with the MEB as an indication of potential gaps in needs being addressed, and to assess the ongoing accuracy of the MEB.
You want to be able to analyse expenditures relating to a specific sector or sectors, for comparison with MEB composition, and potentially to inform programming decisions, for example if unmet needs are identified.

column6: Percentage of households with total monthly expenditure which exceeds the MEB
column7: Pourcentage des ménages ayant un montant total de dépenses dépassant le MEB
column10:
You want a comprehensive understanding of household expenditures and how they prioritize consumption, including total expenditure and spending by category. Categories/types of expenditure can correspond with different sectors.
You want to understand the extent to which total reported spending aligns with the MEB as an indication of potential gaps in needs being addressed, and to assess the ongoing accuracy of the MEB.
You want to be able to analyse expenditures relating to a specific sector or sectors, for comparison with MEB composition, and potentially to inform programming decisions, for example if unmet needs are identified.

column6: Percentage of supported groups self-reporting increased community resilience through GCT projects
column7: Pourcentage de groupes soutenus qui signalent une résilience communautaire accrue grâce aux projets GCT
column10: To measure to which extent grassroots community groups have improved their resilience.

column5: Livelihood Coping Strategies Indicator for Essential Needs
column6: Percentage of households applying Livelihood Coping Strategies (LCS) to meet essential needs, by severity (no use, Stress, Crisis, Emergency)
column7:
Pourcentage de ménages qui appliquent des stratégies d’adaptation des moyens de subsistance
(LCS) pour répondre aux besoins essentiels, par degré de gravité (neutre, stress, crise, urgence)
column10:
The LCS for essential needs can give insight into the underlying factors constraining households’ ability to meet essential needs. Use this indicator if you want to better understand and track the use of coping strategies which impact the livelihoods and dignity of individuals within a household. Resorting to these types of coping mechanisms negatively affects a household’s mid to long-term capacity to generate an income and sustain livelihoods. This in turn means they may be less able to cope when faced with future hardships.

While this indicator can be used as a proxy of household ability to meet essential needs, it cannot detect the extent to which households are able to meet their needs and should be analyzed in tandem with other indicators.

column5: Women's Decision Making: Frequency of Involvement
column6: Frequency with which women are involved in decision making on the use of cash transfers
column7: Fréquence à laquelle les femmes participent à la prise de décisions quant à l’utilisation des transferts monétaires
column10:
You want to better understand how decision-making on the use of cash transfers is determined at household level, and the extent to which there is (or isn’t) a change in women’s decision-making. These indicators should not be applied with women headed households (see analysis section below).

Note: MPC on its own is not sufficient to achieve empowerment; this indicator may be more meaningful for interventions combined with other program activities for the same recipients. Additionally, gendered spending patterns vary by context and expense; a baseline and gender analysis will help contextualize results. Equally important is to design an action that takes into consideration gender in the process of a program with CVA. For a full understanding, this indicator must be paired with protection indicators.

column6: Percentage of households where women are involved in decision making on the use of cash transfers
column7: Pourcentage de ménages où les femmes participent à la prise de décisions quant à l’utilisation des transferts monétaires
column10:
You want to better understand how decision-making on the use of cash transfers is determined at household level, and the extent to which there is (or isn’t) a change in women’s decision-making. These indicators should not be applied with women headed households (see analysis section below).

Note: MPC on its own is not sufficient to achieve empowerment; this indicator may be more meaningful for interventions combined with other program activities for the same recipients. Additionally, gendered spending patterns vary by context and expense; a baseline and gender analysis will help contextualize results. Equally important is to design an action that takes into consideration gender in the process of a program with CVA. For a full understanding, this indicator must be paired with protection indicators.

column6: % of the target population who reported that accessing vendors to use the provided [specify: vouchers / bankcards / cash] was easy
column7: % de la population cible déclarant que l’accès aux commerçants permettant d’utiliser les [spécifiez : bons/ cartes bancaires/ espèces] fournis était facile
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of people who received cash & voucher assistance (CVA) who did not experience any significant difficulties related to the physical, social, and security-related aspects of travelling from their (temporary) homes to the sellers to use the provided vouchers / cash / other modality.

column5: Awareness of Cash & Voucher Assistance Programme
column6: % of the recipients demonstrating clear awareness of key cash & voucher assistance programme information
column7: % de bénéficiaires démontrant une bonne connaissance des informations clés du programme d’assistance en espèces
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of the CVA assistance recipients demonstrating awareness of the key information related to the provided assistance, such as targeting criteria/eligibility, conditions (for conditional cash), how much they get (transfer grant size), when they will get it (period and frequency), when the payments will end, vendor locations (for voucher programmes) and awareness of the complaint and response mechanism. The indicator is not specific to a CVA programme and can also be used in other contexts.

column5: Awareness of Community Feedback and Response Mechanism
column6: % of [specify the target group] who know how to use the community feedback and response mechanism
column7: % de [spécifiez le groupe cible] qui savent comment utiliser le mécanisme de retour d'information et de réponse de la communauté
column10: The indicator measures the extent to which the target group members (and/or any other stakeholders) are aware of the community feedback and response mechanism (CFRM) of a given organization and know how to use it for providing their feedback on the organization's activities.

column6: % of the CVA recipients who were able to influence how the assistance will be used
column7: % de bénéficiaires d’assistance en espèces qui ont pu influencer la manière dont l’assistance a été utilisée
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of recipients of cash & voucher assistance (CVA) who were able to influence how the CVA will be used. It is relevant especially in situations when cash is given to people who might be subjected to unequal decision-making powers within their household (primarily women). It helps you assess whether the recipients were able to use the provided assistance as they needed.

column6: % of [select: cash transfers / vouchers] provided in line with the pre-defined performance criteria
column7: % de [sélectionnez: transferts d’espèces / bons] fournis en accord avec les critères de performance prédéfinis
column10: This composite indicator enables you to measure the proportion of the provided cash-based assistance (CBA) meeting pre-defined performance criteria, such as being provided to the right person, in the correct amount, or according to the established timeframe.

column6: % of respondents who reported that using [specify: vouchers / bank cards / …] was easy
column7: % de répondants déclarant qu’utiliser [spécifiez: espèces/ cartes bancaires/ …] était facile
column10: This indicator measures the proportion of people who spent cash & voucher assistance (CVA) who did not experience any significant problems when redeeming the vouchers / bankcards / cash in other than local currency / other modality. It focuses primarily on issues related to technical problems, beneficiaries’ ability to use the modality and acceptability by the participating vendors.

column6: the beneficiaries’ average travel costs incurred when accessing and using the provided [specify: vouchers / cash / …]
column7: frais moyens de transport occasionnés par les bénéficiaires afin d’accéder et utiliser les [spécifiez: bons/ espèces/…] fournis
column10: The indicator measures the beneficiaries’ average travel costs spent on accessing and redeeming the provided cash & voucher assistance (CVA) for the desired goods (or services). It shows whether the selected modality incurred any significant costs for the beneficiaries and helps with increasing the efficiency and appropriateness of the provided assistance.

column6: number of households receiving cash transfers in the planned amount
column7: nombre de ménages recevant des transferts d’argent selon le montant prévu
column10: This indicator shows the number of households that have received support through cash transfers or vouchers.

column5: Number of Cash for Work Projects
column6: number of community projects completed through Cash for Work
column7: nombre de projets communautaires réalisés au travers du Travail contre Argent (Cash for Work)
column10: This indicator seeks to measure the social or community results of Cash for Work (CfW), in addition to the provision of household income to CfW participants. Examples of CfW projects include clearance of roads following a storm, construction of flood protection measures, or rehabilitating a public space.

column5: Number of Households Supported to Meet Basic Needs
column6: number of households that received [specify the %] of the Minimum Expenditure Basket value for [specify the duration]
column7: nombre de ménages ayant reçu [spécifiez le %] de la valeur du Panier de Dépenses Minimum pour [spécifiez la durée]
column10: This indicator, among the most commonly used of all cash-based assistance indicators, shows the number of households that have received a certain percentage of the Minimum Expenditure Basket’s (MEB) value through cash transfers or vouchers for the intended period. The MEB value estimates the cost of the "basic needs", such as food, shelter, and other “basic needs” of disaster-affected communities, such as health and education.

column5: Operation of the Community Feedback and Response Mechanism
column6: % of inputs received through the community feedback and response mechanism responded to in line with the required procedures
column7: % des contributions reçues par le biais du mécanisme de retour d'information et de réponse de la communauté auxquelles il a été apporté une réponse conformément aux procédures requises
column10: The indicator measures how effectively the community feedback and response mechanism (CFRM) responds to the feedback made by the affected population.

column6: % of households who report experiencing any problem(s) related to getting their cash/voucher
column7: Pourcentage de ménages signalant avoir rencontré des problèmes liés à l'obtention de leur argent/bon
column10: To measure to which extent people have experienced problems to receive CVA. This might be related to e.g. issues getting to or from the distribution point.

column6: % of households who report receiving the correct amount of cash transfers/vouchers
column7: Pourcentage de ménages déclarant avoir reçu le montant correct de transferts d'argent/bons
column10: To measure if recipients have received the value that they were told they would receive.

column6: % of households who received their cash transfers/vouchers in accordance with established timeline
column7: Pourcentage de ménages ayant reçu leurs transferts d'argent/bons conformément au calendrier établi
column10: To measure if people have received their CVA in time.

column6: Total USD value of <cash/vouchers> transferred to recipients
column7: Valeur totale en dollars américains des <espèces/bons> transférés aux bénéficiaires
column10: To measure the total value of distributed CVA.

column6: % of the target population reporting sellers’ inability to offer them the required essential goods
column7: % de la population cible faisant état de l’incapacité des commerçants à leur offrir les produits essentiels nécessaires
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of people who received cash-based assistance (CBA) but were not able to purchase the most essential goods due to inadequate supply.

column6: % of the [specify: voucher / cash / …] recipients who reported experiencing tensions or conflicts due to the provided assistance
column7: % de bénéficiaires de [spécifiez: bons / espèces / …] déclarant avoir fait face à des tensions ou conflits à cause de l’assistance fournie
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of people who experienced conflicts (physical, verbal or other) or tensions related to them receiving cash-based assistance (CBA). It is an important process indicator helping aid agencies identify and mitigate certain negative consequences of their assistance.

column6: Percent of recipients (disaggregated by sex, age, and disability) reporting that humanitarian assistance is delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable, and participatory manner
column7: Pourcentage de bénéficiaires (ventilé par sexe, âge et handicap) ayant déclaré que l’aide humanitaire est fournie de manière sécuritaire, accessible, responsable et participative
column10:
It is recommended to include a Protection Mainstreaming process indicator in all actions providing MPC to affected populations. The purpose of this indicator is to facilitate the operationalisation of all four elements of protection mainstreaming and provide a way to measure the identification, implementation and monitoring of required corrective actions/measures. The overall goal is to have a positive impact on how the assistance is
delivered during the action.

column6: Percentage of school age children enrolled in education
column7: Pourcentage d’enfants d’âge scolaire scolarisés dans l’enseignement
column10: To measure the sector-specific outcome of CVA assistance in education.

column6: Percentage of school age children who attend education over a specific time frame
column7: Pourcentage d’enfants d’âge scolaire qui suivent un enseignement pendant une période de temps donnée
column10: To measure sector-specific outcomes of CVA related to education.

column6: % of households in the highest Coping Strategy Index score category
column7: % de ménages dans la catégorie la plus élevée de l'Indice de Stratégie de Survie
column10: The Coping Strategy Index (CSI) is an indicator of a household’s food security assessing the extent to which households use harmful coping strategies when they do not have enough food or enough money to buy food. The result is reported by a numeric score.

column6: % of the target population with acceptable Food Consumption Score (FCS)
column7: % de la population cible ayant un Score de Consommation Alimentaire acceptable (SCA)
column10: The Food Consumption Score (FCS) is a more complex indicator of a household's food security status, as it considers not only dietary diversity and food frequency but also the relative nutritional importance of different food groups (on the other hand, its use of relatively long, 7 days recall period, might make the data less precise).

column6: Percentage of households that report pressure to leave their shelter for financial reasons
column7:
Pourcentage de ménages déclarant avoir été contraints de quitter leur logement pour
des raisons financières
column10: To measure outcomes of CVA assistance in terms of shelter.

column6: Percentage of households that report having minimum household items that allow all the following: comfortable sleeping, water and food storage, food preparation, cooking, eating, lighting, and clothing
column7:
Pourcentage de ménages déclarant avoir un accès minimum à des articles domestiques
non alimentaires permettant la totalité de ce qui suit : dormir confortablement, stocker l’eau et la nourriture, préparer la no
column10: To measure sector-specific outcomes of CVA assistance related to NFI.

column6: Percentage of households that report living in a shelter that has all the following: adequate space, feels safe, feels private and protected from the weather.
column7: Pourcentage de ménages déclarant vivre dans un abri présentant toutes les caractéristiques suivantes : espace adéquat (dignité), sentiment de sécurité physique, intimité et protection contre les intempéries.
column10: To measure sector-specific outcomes of CVA assistance related to shelter.

column6: Percentage of households that report that their shelter feels warm enough at night
column7: Pourcentage de ménages déclarant que leurs abris sont suffisamment chauds la nuit
column10: To measure sector-specific outcomes of CVA assistance related to shelter.

column6: average value of the Reduced Coping Strategies Index
column7: valeur moyenne de l’Indice de Stratégie de Survie
column10: The Reduced Coping Strategies Index (RCSI) is a proxy indicator of household food insecurity. It considers both the frequency and severity of five pre-selected coping strategies that the household used in the seven days prior to the survey. It is a simplified version of the full Coping Strategies Index indicator.

Percentage of HH having access to a functioning handwashing facility with water and 
soap at home and essential hygiene items including menstrual hygiene products
column7:
Pourcentage de ménages ayant accès à un poste de lavage des mains en état de marche avec de l’eau et du savon à domicile ainsi qu’à des articles d’hygiène essentiels, comme notamment 
des produits d’hygiè
column10: To measure outcomes of Cash & Voucher Assistance (CVA) related to WASH, more specifically hygiene

column6: Percentage of households (HH) reporting that all HH members have access to a safe, secure, clean, and well-maintained toilet, including water or anal cleansing materials
column7: Pourcentage de ménages (HH) déclarant que tous les membres du ménage ont accès à des toilettes sûres, sécurisées, propres et bien entretenues, avec de l’eau ou du matériel pour le nettoyage anal
column10: To measure sectoral outcomes of Cash & Voucher Assistance related to WASH, more specifically sanitation.

column6:
Percentage of households (HH) reporting that all HH members have access to an adequate 
quantity of safe water for drinking, cooking, personal and domestic hygiene
column7: Pourcentage de ménages (HH) déclarant que tous les membres du ménage ont accès à une quantité adéquate d’eau potable pour boire, cuisiner, assurer leur hygiène personnelle et domestique
column10: To measure sectoral outcomes of Cash & Voucher Assistance (CVA) related to WASH, more specifically water supply.

column6: % of project evaluations that include a question related to Climate Resilience.
column7: % d'évaluations de projets comprenant une question relative à la résilience climatique.
column10: Measure the relative number of project evaluations taking Climate Resilience into account. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report

column6: % of current projects that utilize the EST tool
column7: % des projets en cours qui utilisent l'outil EST
column10: Measure the relative number of projects taking Climate Resilience into account. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report.

The indicator measures the learning benefits of any knowledge and skills-transfer activities, such as training or workshops. Not only can it be used for a single activity (e.g. training), but also for the sum of different knowledge and skills-transfer activities.

The indicator measures the learning benefits of any knowledge and skills-transfer activities, such as training or workshops. Not only can it be used for a single activity (e.g. training), but also for the sum of different knowledge and skills-transfer activities.
This indicator shows the extent to which the people targeted by environmental mainstreaming (such as the project staff) follow the promoted environmental practices.

The indicator measures the extent to which the target group members correctly use the desired climate change adaptation measures (such as using drought-tolerant crops, construction of retention ditches, participating in early warning systems, using crop insurance, adopting rainwater harvesting systems, etc.). It is a key indicator of climate change adaptation interventions.

The indicator measures the extent to which the target group members correctly use the desired climate-smart / sustainable / environmentally friendly / other agronomic practices (such as practices reducing erosion / retaining water in soil / increasing the content of nutrients in an environmentally friendly manner, etc.).

column5: Amount of Greenhouse Gas Emissions Saved
column10: The indicator measures the extent to which an intervention contributed to climate change mitigation by reducing the amount of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2-eq) within the stated period. This can be achieved through reducing the usage of fossil fuels, reforestation, improved management of organic waste, reducing the use of fertilizers containing nitrogen and other high-impact measures.

The indicator shows the extent to which the intervention sustainably reduced the use of natural or man-made resources within a given period. This can include fuel (firewood, charcoal, kerosene, petrol, etc.), electricity, water, food waste, plastic, construction materials and other resources whose use contributes to depleting the natural resource base.

column5: Area of Land Under Improved Management
column10: The indicator assesses the total area of land (including forests, pastures, fields, etc.) that are managed using environmentally beneficial practices, such as the application of organic inputs, use of minimum tillage, planting of cover crops, use of bylaws / regulations and other environmentally sustainable and economically viable practices.

The indicator assesses the proportion of target farmers who are aware of the promoted agronomic practices and their main benefits (a similar indicator can be used for any other target group). Such data helps you design the focus of your promotion activities and evaluate their effectiveness and reach.

column6: % of the target households perceiving a high likelihood of being severely affected by [specify the climate hazard]
column7: % des ménages cibles percevant une probabilité élevée d'être gravement touchés par [précisez le risque climatique]
column10: The indicator identifies the extent to which the target households feel vulnerable to a given hazard (for example, droughts, heat waves, floods). Theoretically, the more prepared a household is, the less vulnerable it should feel.

column6: Level of integration of climate risks in the sectoral interventions in a project
column7: Niveau d'intégration des risques climatiques dans les interventions sectorielles d'un projet.
column10: The indicator identifies the extent to which climate risks are integrated in the sectoral interventions in a project to enhance climate resilience. The indicator can be used for internal evaluations

column6: Level of utilisation of the Environmental Stewardship Tool (EST) in a project.
column7: Niveau d’utilisation de l’outil de gestion environnementale (EST) dans un projet.
column10: The indicator identifies the extent to which the Environmental Stewardship Tool (EST) was utilized in a project to identify and mitigate environmental risks. The indicator can be used for internal evaluations

This indicator is relevant when people targeted by environmental mainstreaming measures (e.g. project staff, partners) need specific knowledge or skills to practice the promoted practices. It measures the extent to which they have such knowledge or skills. Examples include knowing how to effectively consider environmental impact in procurement, segregate waste, or reduce energy consumption.

The indicator measures people’s perceptions of how effective the promoted agronomic practices are. Such data is very important, as people are not likely to adopt practices that – in their opinion – do not work. The data can help you design the focus of your promotion activities and evaluate their effectiveness.

column6: % of target population reporting preparedness to face [specify the given climate hazard]
column7: % de la population cible déclarant être prêt à faire face à [précisez le danger donné]
column10: The indicator identifies the extent to which the target population feels prepared to face a specific climate hazard. Theoretically, the more prepared people are, the less vulnerable they should feel. It is an important indicator of a climate adaptation or climate resilience intervention’s outcome.

column6: % of [specify the target group] with attitudes supportive of gender equality
column7: % de [spécifiez le groupe cible] ayant des attitudes en faveur de l’égalité de genre
column10: The indicator shows the extent to which the target group members have attitudes supportive of gender equality. It was designed for projects that do not deal with the more sensitive attitudes towards sexual and gender-based violence. If you also need to measure such attitudes, use the more comprehensive indicator “Gender Equitable Men (GEM) Scale” available at IndiKit.

column6: % of target [choose: men / women] who have supporting attitudes towards women’s political participation
column7: % de [choisir: hommes / femmes] manifestant du soutien envers la participation des femmes à la vie politique
column10: The indicator shows the extent to which the target group members are supportive of women’s active political participation.

column6: average score on Household Decision-Making Index
column7: score moyen sur l’Index de prise de décision des ménages
column10: Women’s decision-making power is one of the key aspects of gender equality. This indicator therefore measures the level of women’s involvement in household decision-making regarding consumption and expenditures, reproductive choices, and other decisions.

column6: average value of the Women’s Autonomy Index
column7: valeur moyenne de l’Index de l’autonomie des femmes
column10: This indicator measures the extent of women’s autonomy manifested through several key dimensions, such as their access to income, mobility, freedom of expression, and others.

column6: % of women participating in community groups
column7: % de femmes participant à des groupes communautaires
column10: Women’s participation in community groups is an important empowering factor as it enables women to increase their social capital and helps them to gain new knowledge, receive support, access a range of services (such as access to finance), and advocate for the required changes.

column5: Women’s Representation in Community Groups’ Management
column6: % of [specify the community group] with at least XX% of actively participating female representatives
column7: % de [spécifier le groupe communautaire] comprenant au moins XX% de représentants féminins participant activement
column10: Women’s active participation in the management structures of the community-based groups is an important indicator of women’s empowerment and gender equality. The indicator therefore assesses the proportion of community groups (such as water management groups) with a minimum, pre-set percentage of actively participating female representatives.

column6: % of target [choose: men / women] with supportive attitudes towards women’s economic participation
column7: % de [choisir: hommes / femmes] ciblés manifestant du soutien envers la participation des femmes à la vie économique
column10: The indicator shows the extent to which your target group members are supportive of women's active economic participation. It helps understand how target groups react to an intervention and change their attitudes toward women's economic participation.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column5: Implementation of Gender and Age Mainstreaming Measures
column6: % of planned gender and age mainstreaming measures that were implemented throughout the project
column7: % des mesures d'intégration des questions de genre et d'âge prévues qui ont été mises en œuvre tout au long du projet
column10: This indicator measures the extent to which the planned gender and age mainstreaming measures were implemented. It is one of the key gender and age mainstreaming indicators.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column5: Implementation of Social Inclusion Mainstreaming Measures
column6: % of planned measures for mainstreaming social inclusion that were implemented
column7: % des mesures prévues pour l'intégration des questions d'inclusion sociale qui ont été mises en œuvre
column10: This indicator assesses the extent to which the planned measures for mainstreaming social inclusion were implemented. It is one of the key social inclusion mainstreaming indicators.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column6: % of [specify a vulnerable group] who believe that people had a similar opportunity to benefit from the project irrespective of their [specify: gender / age / other]
column7: % de [spécifier un groupe vulnérable] qui pensent que les personnes ont eu les mêmes chances de bénéficier du projet, indépendamment de leur [spécifier : genre / âge / autre]
column10: The indicator assesses the perceptions of vulnerable groups, such as women or elderly people, who think that people had similar access to the project’s assistance, irrespective of their gender / age / other factors. It helps you understand the extent to which they feel that the assistance was delivered fairly and inclusively.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column5: Use of Gender and Age Analysis
column6: % of gender and age mainstreaming measures suggested by a conducted gender and age analysis included in the project implementation
column7: % de mesures d'intégration des questions de genre et d'âge résultant d’une analyse de genre et d'âge qui ont été incluses dans la mise en œuvre du projet
column10: This indicator highlights the extent to which gender and age mainstreaming measures proposed based on a conducted analysis were included in the project implementation. It helps ensure that the analysis is used. It should always be used together with an indicator that measures the extent to which a project’s gender and age mainstreaming measures were actually implemented.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column6: % of beneficiaries reporting that humanitarian assistance is delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable, and participatory manner
column7: % de bénéficiaires déclarant que l'aide humanitaire est fournie de manière sûre, accessible, responsable et participative
column10: Protection of the emergency-affected population is one of the key aspects of humanitarian assistance. This process indicator developed by DG ECHO therefore focuses on monitoring the extent to which the project beneficiaries felt that the provided assistance was delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable, and participatory manner.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column6: % of [specify gender] reporting that they were able to decide on how the assistance their household received would be used
column7: % de [préciser le genre] déclarant qu'ils ont pu décider de l'utilisation de l'aide que leur ménage a reçu
column10: This indicator measures people’s control over how specific assistance they receive would be used. It is relevant, especially when the assistance is supposed to benefit people who might be subjected to unequal decision-making powers within their household (primarily women). It helps you assess whether the recipients could use the assistance provided as needed.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column6: number of communities where key barriers to participation faced by specific groups were assessed in a participatory manner
column7: nombre de communautés dans lesquelles les principaux obstacles à la participation de groupes spécifiques ont été évalués de manière participative
column10: This indicator is designed for projects working in various geographic communities – e.g. villages or parts of urban areas. It measures in how many of such communities, the project tried to understand the barriers preventing specific groups of people (e.g. elderly or displaced) from participating in its activities.

column3: Gender, Age and Social Inclusion Mainstreaming
column6: Percent of recipients (disaggregated by sex, age, and disability) reporting that humanitarian assistance is delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable, and participatory manner
column7: Pourcentage de bénéficiaires (ventilé par sexe, âge et handicap) ayant déclaré que l’aide humanitaire est fournie de manière sécuritaire, accessible, responsable et participative
column10:
It is recommended to include a Protection Mainstreaming process indicator in all actions providing MPC to affected populations. The purpose of this indicator is to facilitate the operationalisation of all four elements of protection mainstreaming and provide a way to measure the identification, implementation and monitoring of required corrective actions/measures. The overall goal is to have a positive impact on how the assistance is
delivered during the action.

column6: % of [choose: men / women] who say that wife beating is acceptable
column7: % de [choisir: hommes / femmes] qui affirment que battre les femmes est acceptable
column10: This indicator measures the proportion of either men or women who consider wife beating as an acceptable way of treating wives.

column5: Awareness of Available Support for GBV survivors
column6: % of women aware of where women affected by GBV can access the required support
column7: % de femmes qui savent à quel endroit les femmes victimes de violence basée sur le genre peuvent obtenir le soutien nécessaire
column10: The available data show that a large proportion of women living in low-income countries have at some point in their life experienced gender based violence. Awareness of available support is an important pre-condition for women accessing the assistance they need. Therefore, this indicator measures the proportion of women that are aware of where women affected by gender based violence can access the required support

column6: % of women aged 15 - 49 who experienced severe physical violence in the past 12 months
column7: % de femmes âgées de 15 à 49 ans ayant subi des violences physiques graves au cours des 12 derniers mois
column10: Freedom from violence is a critical aspect of women’s empowerment and greater gender equality. This indicator therefore measures the proportion of women who in the past 12 months experienced severe physical violence. Considering how sensitive (and in some ways also demanding) the collection of the required data is, it should be used only in interventions that are specifically addressing the prevention and response to gender-based violence.

column6: % of women aged 15 - 49 who experienced sexual violence in the past 12 months
column7: % de femmes âgées de 15 à 49 ans victimes de violence sexuelle au cours des 12 derniers mois
column10: Freedom from violence is a critical aspect of women’s empowerment and greater gender equality. This indicator therefore measures the proportion of women who in the past 12 months experienced sexual violence. Considering how sensitive the collection of the data required for this indicator is, this indicator should be used only in interventions that are specifically addressing the prevention and response to sexual violence.

column6: % of project evaluations that include a question related to Gender, Diversity and Inclusion.
column7: % d'évaluations de projets comprenant une question relative au genre, à la diversité et à l'inclusion.
column10: Measure the relative number of project evaluations taking GDI into account. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report

column5: Use of a Gender, Inclusion or Power Analysis
column6: % of projects that utilize a gender, inclusion or power analysis.
column7: % de projets qui utilisent une analyse de genre, d'inclusion ou de pouvoir.
column10: Measure the relative number of project that use the input of an analysis related to GDI. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report.

column6: % of respondents aware of the promoted [specify the product / service]
column7: % de répondants connaissant l’existence du [spécifiez le produit / service] promu
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of the target group members who are aware of the promoted product or service. It helps you understand the effectiveness and reach of any promotional activities or initiatives to strengthen the marketing competencies of supported sellers / service providers.

column6: Average social distance score
column7: Score moyen de distance sociale
column10: The indicator calculates a social distance score by using the Bogardus social distance scale, which measures people's willingness to participate in varying levels of social contact with members of marginalized groups, such as certain ethnic minorities or people with a disability.

column6: % of vulnerable target group members aware of their promoted rights
column7: % des membres du groupe cible vulnérable conscients de leurs droits promus
column10: The indicator assesses the proportion of people from a specific vulnerable group (such as people with disabilities or ethnic minorities) aware of the promoted rights.

column6: the average Access Score provided by [specify the vulnerable group] on their access to the targeted services
column7: le Score d'Accès moyen fourni par [précisez le groupe vulnérable] sur leur accès aux services ciblés
column10: The indicator assesses to what extent the members of a marginalized group feel they can access a pre-defined set of basic services.

column5: Staff Understanding of Mainstreaming Social Inclusion
column6: % of staff who understand the key principles and practices of mainstreaming social inclusion
column7: % des membres du personnel qui comprend les principes et pratiques clés de l'intégration des questions d'inclusion sociale
column10: The indicator assesses to what extent the staff (of an organization or a specific project only) understand the key principles and practices of mainstreaming social inclusion. It indicates the extent to which they can support the effective implementation of measures for mainstreaming social inclusion. The indicator can also highlight the need for (further) staff training on specific topics relating to mainstreaming social inclusion.

column6: % of staff with supportive attitudes towards gender equality
column7: % du personnel ayant une attitude favorable envers l'égalité des genres
column10: This indicator helps you understand the extent to which the staff - of an organization or a specific project - have attitudes that support gender equality (and can therefore work on promoting it in their work). It can also identify any needs for working with the staffs’ existing attitudes.

column5: Understanding of Gender and Age Mainstreaming
column6: % of staff who understand the key principles and practices of gender and age mainstreaming
column7: % des membres du personnel qui comprend les principes et pratiques clés de l'intégration des questions de genre et d'âge
column10: This indicator assesses the extent to which the staff (of an organization or a specific project only) understand the key principles and practices of gender and age mainstreaming. It indicates how much they can support the effective implementation of gender and age mainstreaming measures. The indicator can also highlight the need for (further) staff training on specific topics relating to gender and age mainstreaming.

column6: % of project staff aware of the key principles and practices of protection mainstreaming
column7: % du personnel du projet connaissant les principes et pratiques essentiels à l'intégration de la protection
column10: The indicator assesses the extent to which the staff who work on implementing a project understand the key principles and practices of protection mainstreaming. The indicator can highlight the need for (further) staff training, in cases where the data shows a limited understanding of protection mainstreaming principles and practice.

column5: % of Country Budget to Local Partners
column6: % of realized country budget to local partners
column7: % du budget national réalisé pour les partenaires locaux
column10: Measure the relative amount of budget allocated to local partners. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report.

column5: Cash Directly Received by Local Groups
column6: % of a realized country budget is directly received as cash by local groups
column7: % du budget national réalisé est directement reçu en espèces par les groupes locaux
column10: Measure the relative amount of budget allocated to local groups. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report.

column6: % of proposals where local partners were involved in the design phase.
column7: % de propositions dans lesquelles les partenaires locaux ont été impliqués dans la phase de conception.
column10: Measure the relative number of proposals in which local partners have participated during the design of the intervention. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report.

column6: % of project evaluations that include a question related to Peace Nexus.
column7: % d'évaluations de projets comprenant une question relative aux Nexus de Paix.
column10: Measure the relative number of project evaluations taking Peace Nexus into account. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report

column6: % of current projects that include a peace/conflict related indicator.
column7: % des projets en cours qui comprennent un indicateur lié à la paix/aux conflits.
column10: Measure the relative number of projects including an indicator on Peace Nexus. The indicator value must be reported in the Quarterly Country Report

column5: Absence of Tensions or Conflicts due to Assistance Provided
column6: The percentage of target group members who did not experience conflict, disagreements, tensions or violence (physical, verbal, psychological, emotional or other) related to them receiving the provided assistance.
column7: Absence de tensions ou de conflits dus à l'assistance fournie
column10: The indicator measures the proportion of target group members who did not experience conflict, disagreements, tensions or violence (physical, verbal, psychological, emotional or other) related to them receiving the provided assistance. It is an important process indicator helping aid agencies identify and mitigate against the potentially negative consequences of their assistance.

column5: Perception of Social Cohesion and Trust
column6: % of population that perceive an improvement in social cohesion and trust across conflict lines or groups with diverse (ethnic/religious/political) background
column7: % de la population qui perçoit une amélioration de la cohésion sociale et de la confiance au-delà des lignes de conflit ou des groupes d'origines (ethniques/religieuses/politiques) diverses
column10: This indicator aims to measure people's perception of social cohesion and trust, which are often seriously damaged after conflict.
